questions.question: Why are civil and political rights called "first generation" rights?
options: They were the first category of rights to gain widespread recognition
They are the least important rights
They were created in the 21st century
They apply only to the first generation of citizens
questions.explanation: Civil and political rights are "first generation" rights because they were the first to receive widespread recognition.

questions.question: Under international law, restrictions on freedom of expression must be:
options: Prescribed by law, necessary, and for a legitimate purpose
Decided arbitrarily by officials
Permanent and unconditional
Applied only to journalists
questions.explanation: Restrictions must be prescribed by law, necessary for a legitimate purpose (e.g. national security, public order), not arbitrary.

questions.question: Which right is described as absolute, with no permitted restrictions?
options: The prohibition of torture
Freedom of movement
The right to assembly
The right to property
questions.explanation: The prohibition of torture is an absolute right that cannot be restricted under any circumstances.

questions.question: What does the "presumption of innocence" mean?
options: Every person is innocent until proven guilty
The accused must prove their own innocence
Judges decide guilt before a trial
Only the wealthy are presumed innocent
questions.explanation: The presumption of innocence — a key element of a fair trial — means every person is innocent until proven guilty.

questions.question: What is "habeas corpus"?
options: The right to challenge the legality of one's detention before a court
The right to free healthcare
The right to own property
The right to vote at 16
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus is the right to challenge the legality of one's detention before a court.
